g.text: six modalities · one repository each · services beside them
blue = repository (passive) · green = service (logic) · pink = the delta from today
memory, per pass · the planner holds it
which FILES each public graph came from
what this agent's own graphs ARE
a derived view, so it stays
never mutated — a world is a value
wraps one, scopes it to this agent
`Desires.rebuild()` is a service inside a repository.
intent is right — *the runtime is read-only* — but it is kept
true by hiding the writer inside, not by layering.
A repository is built two ways here, and both are fine.
`Beliefs`, `Desires` and `Intentions` WRAP a Store and delegate;
`Imaginarium` and `_Derivation` EXTEND one. The imaginarium is
a full repository — its own domain method is `reached()`, which
mints the graph for a search node.
The menu repo holds TEMPLATES, never rows.
runs each template's `orexis:available` per ask and returns
`list[Affordance]`. A row exists exactly while its premise
holds (#263), and `$state` is a parameter so the planner can
ask for the menu of an IMAGINED world. Storing rows would
break the search; storing templates is what the table meant.
a discharged debt and a revision are all *what I DID*, and
today they stay in the live ledgers — so a paid debt and a
forgotten one look alike. Nothing points INTO history: what
must outlive the ring is copied at commit time, as an
modality by its class, so the imaginarium — but it must
SURVIVE the pass, because metrics read it. History is the
likely home; #311 does not name it.
provenance, classification, actions and desire/asserted at
birth — an arrow into nearly everything, which said nothing.
